title: O, Speed Thee, Christian, on Thy Way
description: O, Speed Thee, Christian, on Thy Way in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 316, “The Whole Armor of the Lord”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, speed thee, Chris-tian, on thy way! And to thine ar-mor cling; With gird-ed loins the call o-bey That love and mer-cy bring!

lines: O, speed thee, Christian, on thy way!
With girded loins the call obey
There is a battle to be fought,
A crown of glory to be sought,
O, faint not, Christian! for thy sighs
The race must come before the prize,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
